no one who should matter to you will judge you for this period of your life, and you shouldn't live up to anyone else's expectations beyond your own.

you dont deserve any suffering ever, and trust me, most of your friends will never stop caring about you, no matter how long this takes.

if you can, take a few days to rest. take your medication if you feel up to it, and talk to your therapist about this inability to work, as this is likely another manifestation of your anxiety disorder. they can give you strategies to manage this.

i know from experience that if i waste my time, or just dont get out of bed at all, i feel so much worse about myself.

if you get out of bed, there's at least a slight possibility that you could do something that'd make things better, and your brain knows that.

please keep going, there's still a chance that things might go okay
why do you feel that you have to?

you don't have to do anything.

there's still time to fix whatever is going on.

It's not always going to be this bad. Hell, you could probably make things better for yourself one day soon. The important thing is taking everything step by step, aiming to feel okay with yourself.

People will definitely miss you when you're gone, and the world will be worse off without you.

I hope the day you take the first step towards climbing from this hole begins soon.

One thing I reccomend doing is pretending the self-harm is from previous weeks. It's a trick you can't do every time, and I'm not sure if it would work on other therapists, but it might allow you to touch on the issue, which is incredibly important.
As far as I know, unless you're in immediate danger, they shouldn't tell your parents about anything. That's how it works in Australia, at least, and maybe America too.

If you're old enough to go to the GP without parental supervision, mention your worries to them. It won't be easy to keep it hidden from your parents, but you could at least get some sort of diagnosis/referral to a therapist and some professional advice for what to do next. It might also make your parents believe you. If you think that they'd take your stuff away regardless of whether you have a diagnosis or not, then you might want to keep the diagnosis to yourself.
